entry.title: Can a network whose trunk is only XOR, table lookups and integer adds learn Connect Four?
entry.content: Can a network whose trunk is only XOR, table lookups and integer adds learn Connect Four? Partly. I trained a GF(2⁸) integer model (8.4M params, CPU-only) on 320k games labelled by a negamax search teacher. What it learned: • agrees with the teacher on 59.6% of training / 41.0% of board-disjoint holdout positions • beats a random player 85.2% of the time What it didn't: • loses to a 1-ply "win now / block now" rule (wins 37.2%) • loses to 2-ply lookahead (wins 24.3%) Agreeing with a teacher is not the same as playing well, and this release measures both. entry.title: Maverick 1.1 is out.
entry.content: Maverick 1.1 is out. When we released the first version, the feedback was clear: real people do not give one clean command at a time. They change their minds, they point and say "put that on the shelf", they ask for a lamp that is in another room, and sometimes the one speaking is a remote expert helping someone on site. 1.1 is built around exactly that. - Say "no, the other one" and it undoes the last action and repeats it on the other object. If the effect can't be undone, like a button that was already pressed, it tells you. - It sees what people are looking at or pointing at, and who is speaking. - It finds objects in other rooms, goes there and acts, or asks which one if there are two.

Three matchup cells are measured: vs Mihawk 67%, vs Nico Robin 60%, and the Sabo mirror at 50%. The useful part for anyone tracking deck performance: log game results, let the math tell you when a verdict is real vs noise. One season of games is enough to get 3-5 measured mat
